title: The futur simple
goal: Form the futur simple of regular verbs and use it for plans, schedules and promises, for example about a new job.

items.en: futur simple of regular verbs: infinitive + -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont

drills.en: You will start on Monday, March 3.
I will work from Monday to Friday.

drills.text: Nous ___ la semaine par un dîner d'équipe. (finir)
drills.en: We will end the week with a team lunch.

items.en: futur simple of -re verbs: drop the final e

drills.en: She will wait for her colleagues on Monday.

drills.prompt: In a formal email from Human Resources, which is most typical?
drills.explain: Written, formal schedules usually use the futur simple. Commenciez is the imparfait.

drills.prompt: Which one is the futur simple?
drills.explain: -rai = futur simple. -ais = imparfait. vais + infinitive = futur proche.

blocks.title: An email from Human Resources
blocks.context: Karim has a new job in a distribution centre in Laval. He receives this email.
blocks.fr:
Objet : Votre première semaine
Bonjour Karim,
Bienvenue dans l'équipe ! Voici quelques informations pour votre première semaine.
Vous commencerez le lundi 3 mars à 8 h 30. Vous travaillerez du lundi au vendredi, de 8 h 30 à 16 h 30.
Le premier jour, vous rencontrerez votre superviseure, Mme Tremblay, et toute l'équipe. Ensuite, vous suivrez une formation de trois jours.
Vous prendrez votre pause du midi à 12 h. Vendredi, nous finirons la semaine par un dîner d'équipe.
N'oubliez pas d'apporter une pièce d'identité.
À lundi !
Julie Bérubé, Ressources humaines
blocks.en:
Subject: Your first week
Hello Karim,
Welcome to the team! Here is some information for your first week.
You will start on Monday, March 3, at 8:30 a.m. You will work Monday to Friday, from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
On the first day, you will meet your supervisor, Ms. Tremblay, and the whole team. Then you will take a three-day training course.
You will take your lunch break at noon. On Friday, we will end the week with a team lunch.
Don't forget to bring a piece of ID.
See you Monday!
Julie Bérubé, Human Resources

blocks.title: One verb, one word
blocks.body:
The **futur simple** is a one-word future: [[je travaillerai]] (I will work). It is common in **writing**, in **formal** language (emails, letters, instructions, schedules), for **promises** and for **predictions**. In conversation, people use it too, especially for things further away or less certain.

The good news: for regular verbs, you already know the base. It is the **infinitive**.

blocks.title: How to form it
blocks.note: The endings are the present tense of **avoir** without the av- of nous and vous: [[ai, as, a, (av)ons, (av)ez, ont]]. Every future stem ends in **r**.

blocks.title: Three regular verbs
head: travailler
finir
prendre
blocks.note: Listen for the **r** before the ending: it is the sound of the future. [[je travaillerai]] ends like *é*; [[ils travailleront]] ends with the nasal *on*.

blocks.title: Futur proche or futur simple?
head: futur proche
futur simple
rows: More written, formal, or for promises
Further away, a prediction, a schedule
Vous trouverez le formulaire en ligne.
blocks.note: Often both are possible and mean almost the same thing. Don't worry about choosing wrongly: you will be understood either way.

blocks.title: Spelling notes
blocks.body:
- **-re verbs** drop the final **e**: [[prendre → prendr-]], [[attendre → attendr-]], [[apprendre → apprendr-]].
- **-er verbs** keep the whole infinitive, even if the e is barely pronounced: [[je travaillerai]], [[j'étudierai]], [[je jouerai]].
- A few -er verbs change their stem, as in the present: [[acheter → j'achèterai]], [[appeler → j'appellerai]]. Learn these two for now; you'll meet others later.

blocks.title: Future, imparfait or present?
blocks.body:
Three forms of the same verb can sound close. Listen for the **r** and the final vowel:

- [[je parle]]: ends in *l*, present
- [[je parlais]]: ends in an open *è*, imparfait
- [[je parlerai]]: has an **r** and ends in a closed *é*, future

In everyday speech, the e in the middle often disappears: [[je travaillerai]] sounds like *travaille-ré*, [[nous parlerons]] like *parl-rons*.

examples.fr: je parle, je parlais, je parlerai
examples.en: I speak, I used to speak, I will speak

blocks.body:
- **Adding an e to -re verbs:** [[je prenderai]] → [[je prendrai]]; [[j'attenderai]] → [[j'attendrai]].
- **Dropping the infinitive:** [[je parlai]] is a different (literary) tense. The future is [[je parlerai]].
- **Changing -ir verbs:** [[je finerai]] → [[je finirai]]. Keep the whole infinitive.
- **Will = vouloir?** No: *I will work* is [[je travaillerai]], not [[je veux travailler]] (I want to work).
- **-ont vs -ons:** [[ils travailleront]] (they), [[nous travaillerons]] (we).

blocks.title: Work words in Québec
blocks.body:
- [[le dîner]] = lunch in Québec, so [[un dîner d'équipe]] is a team **lunch**, and [[la pause du midi]] is the lunch break.
- [[un emploi]] is the neutral word for a job. In informal Québec French, people say [[une job]], and it is feminine: [[J'ai une nouvelle job !]] In France, it is [[un job]] (and the standard word is [[un travail]] or [[un poste]]).
- Québec uses feminine job titles widely: [[une superviseure]], [[une ingénieure]], [[une professeure]].

blocks.prompt: You are the new employee's buddy at work. Write a short, friendly message to welcome them and explain their first day: when they will start, who they will meet, where they will take their break, and one promise.
blocks.promptFr: Écrivez un message de bienvenue à un nouveau collègue.
checklist: At least four verbs in the futur simple
A promise: Je passerai à ton bureau… / On mangera ensemble…

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour Amira, bienvenue dans l'équipe ! Lundi, tu commenceras à 9 h. Le matin, tu rencontreras notre superviseur, M. Gagnon, et tu visiteras le bureau. Nous prendrons la pause du midi ensemble à la cafétéria. L'après-midi, tu commenceras ta formation. Tu finiras à 16 h 30. Je passerai à ton bureau à 10 h pour un café. À lundi ! Lucie
models.en: Hello Amira, welcome to the team! On Monday, you'll start at 9 a.m. In the morning, you'll meet our supervisor, Mr. Gagnon, and you'll visit the office. We'll take our lunch break together in the cafeteria. In the afternoon, you'll start your training. You'll finish at 4:30 p.m. I'll come by your desk at 10 for a coffee. See you Monday! Lucie

blocks.prompt: Make three promises to yourself for your new job or your studies, in about 30 seconds. Use the futur simple.
checklist: Three verbs in the futur simple
A time marker: chaque jour, le lundi, l'année prochaine
A negative: je n'arriverai pas en retard

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Au travail, je n'arriverai jamais en retard. Je parlerai français avec mes collègues tous les jours. Et le vendredi, je prendrai le temps de manger avec l'équipe.
models.en: At work, I will never arrive late. I will speak French with my colleagues every day. And on Fridays, I will take the time to eat with the team.

summary:
- Form the **futur simple** of regular verbs: infinitive + [[-ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont]]; -re verbs drop the e ([[je prendrai]])
- Recognize it by the **r** before the ending: [[je parlerai]] vs [[je parlais]]
- Use it for schedules, formal messages and promises: [[Vous commencerez lundi.]] [[On fêtera ça !]]
